transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-08-05 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 46m
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Dana Price (CTO, Erythra), Marcus Lin (Head of Infra), Priya Khatri (Security), Ruben Ortiz (ML Eng)

Summary/Notes: quick intake. Customer currently on hybrid: some inference on prem for PHI models, a bit of hosted for lower-sensitivity models. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated to standardize and reduce ops overhead; wants isolation guarantees and clear burst behavior for synchronous workloads.

00:00 Dana Price: "Alright thanks everyone for joining, we got about 45 minutes. I'll hand off to Dana to give a quick intro to Erythra and what we're trying to solve."
00:08 Dana Price: "Yeah so Erythra we're a diagnostics start-up, ML models run real-time inference for triage, the thing is spikes are pretty spiky — we have clinical windows with sudden surges. We need predictability; last month our self-hosted cluster saturated and latencies jumped, um, and the throttling made some UXs unusable."
00:26 Maya Chen: "Thanks, Dana. Maya from Redwood — I'll take product/contract questions, Luis will go into the ops and benchmarks. Broadly are you looking for hosted vs dedicated or a private deployment?"
00:37 Marcus Lin: "Mostly dedicated. We like Redwood's managed layer but need tenant isolation and dedicated GPU pools. Also VPC peering/Private link and KMS for keys. We want to avoid any noise from multi-tenant noisy neighbors."
00:50 Luis Ortega: "Totally, we can do dedicated GPU pools with tenant fencing. Quick clarification — when you say spikes how big are they, and are the bursts synchronous (chat style) or async batch?"
01:05 Ruben Ortiz: "Mostly synchronous — doctors using chat assistant during rounds. Peaks are short, like 30s to 5min, but high RPS. Typical requests are 256-512 tokens, some outliers to 1k. We also have nightly bulk rerank jobs but those are lower priority."
01:22 Luis Ortega: "Okay that helps. Our Dedicated offering supports a Warm/Hot pool model — you can reserve baseline nodes and allow burst capacity. For tight latency SLOs we recommend prewarming a hotpool for the chat front end and routing best-effort batch to the reserve. You can also configure fallback to a smaller, quantized model if capacity is constrained."
01:45 Priya Khatri: "What about encryption at rest/in flight and KMS? Our compliance org requires customer-managed keys. Can Redwood Dedicated plug into our KMS/HSM?"
01:55 Maya Chen: "Yes, private deployments and Dedicated for enterprise support customer KMS integrations — S3 encrypted with your keys, and we integrate with common KMS providers. We'll attach the SOC2 and architecture diagrams after the call."
02:04 Priya: "Okay please send that. Also we need audit logs for each inference call — token-level traces, who called what. How granular are your logs?"
02:14 Samir Patel: "We surface per-request metadata in the console — model, route, latency, and token counts. For Dedicated we can add longer retention as an add-on; full PII sweeping is something we advise to route to your audit store."
02:28 Marcus Lin: "Another question — what happens when burst capacity saturates? Does traffic queue, fail, or degrade to another model? We need predictable behavior; we can't have silent degradations."
02:38 Luis Ortega: "Good question. Default is a routing policy: you can set hard limits (reject) or soft degrade — fall back to a smaller variant or a cached response. We recommend a canary fallback chain: primary model -> quantized variant -> cached prefix -> reject with graceful error. We can also configure concurrency limits per tenant to prevent head-of-line blocking."
03:00 Dana Price: "How easy is it to test that? We want to run a benchmark with our real traces to verify SLOs before committing to a reserved pool."
03:08 Luis Ortega: "We usually run two benchmarks: low-latency chat (p95 < target) with concurrent short sequences, and high-throughput burst with realistic RPS spikes. If you share traces, we can replay them in our sandbox or replicate locally with our harness. There may be a small charge for a dedicated benchmark run if it requires ephemeral reserved hardware."
03:30 Ruben Ortiz: "We can anonymize traces, yeah we'll do that. Also curious about model variants — we run a fine-tuned Llama family model and a distilled smaller model. How does quantization affect semantic drift?"
03:44 Luis Ortega: "Quantization can introduce slight differences; our Optimize team profiles models and recommends configurations. For critical outputs we suggest A/Bing with a sample prompt set and gating the fallback. We also have regression alerts tied to evals so you see if the smaller variant drifts."
03:59 Marcus Lin: "Ops question: we want to limit noisy tenants inside our org (multiple teams). Can you do intra-customer isolation?"
04:07 Maya Chen: "Yes, you can implement tenant sharding within your Dedicated allocation — logical isolation per business unit. Each shard gets quota and concurrency rules and you can route based on API keys. That lives on top of reserved nodes so there isn't cross-tenant noisy neighbor at the infra level."
04:21 Dana Price: "Pricing — we need predictability. How do commitments work? If we reserve X GPUs, can we burst beyond for short spikes without big overage shocks?"
04:31 Maya Chen: "Commitments are monthly or annual. You reserve base capacity and we offer burst for short windows at a different rate, typically a higher per-hour cost but subject to availability. There's also a burst-protection add-on (guaranteed prewarm) if you need firm bursts — it's more expensive but gives dedicated prewarmed nodes during your specified windows."
04:55 Priya Khatri: "Procurement — any standard SOC2/ISO attachments and is there an AIDE for redaction?"
05:02 Maya Chen: "We have an enterprise pack with SOC2 Type II artifacts, ISO certs, and a compliance binder. For PHI redaction we recommend edge anonymization or Redwood's pre-processing hooks to strip tokens before logging. We'll include examples in the doc bundle."
05:18 Dana Price: "What SLAs do you guarantee for Dedicated?"
05:21 Maya Chen: "We publish uptime SLAs for the control plane and SLOs for tail latency in the contract. For Dedicated there's a higher SLA tied to reserved capacity. We'll share examples of previous latency profiles in the playbook doc."
05:34 Ruben Ortiz: "Latency profile — can you give ballpark numbers on p95 for 512 token requests on a reserved GPU?"
05:40 Luis Ortega: "Ballpark depends on model size; for a 13B model on A100 class we often see p95 around 200-400ms with our optimized runtime when KV cache hits are high. With cold starts it's more. For 70B it's multiples of that. We'll include measured numbers from our catalog for your model family."
06:05 Marcus Lin: "Is preemption a risk if cloud provider reclaims nodes?"
06:10 Luis Ortega: "On Dedicated we run on reserved instances and our orchestration minimizes preemption. For the highest isolation we offer private on-prem or bring-your-own infra options with less risk of reclaim. But generally preemption is rare and handled with graceful failover."
06:25 Priya Khatri: "Can we enable SSO for Redwood console access and RBAC?"
06:29 Maya Chen: "Yes SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC are standard for enterprise accounts. You can map roles to API keys and routes."
06:38 Dana Price: "Timeline — we're aiming for a pilot in Q4. Procurement in September. Does that align with Redwood onboarding for Dedicated?"
06:46 Maya Chen: "Yep Q4 pilot is feasible. Onboarding takes 4–8 weeks depending on private network setup and compliance work. We'll work with procurement and infra to line things up."
06:55 Ruben Ortiz (overlap): "Question — observability: can we get token-level per-route cost accounting? We need to allocate charges to teams."
07:05 Samir Patel: "We provide token-level cost breakdowns by API key and route. For Dedicated we can push the raw usage logs into your billing bucket for internal chargeback."
07:15 Dana Price: "Anything else around fallback policies? We worry about silent errors when the small model drifts."
07:22 Luis Ortega: "Recommendation: maintain a gated canary where a small percent of traffic goes to the fallback and compare outputs with a regression metric. If drift exceeds threshold, circuit break and alert. We can automate rolls and rollbacks in the console."
07:36 Marcus Lin: "Edge case: what about extremely short but huge bursts — e.g., 10x baseline for 90s during a badge scanning event — we need the UX to remain within 500ms p95 or better. Is that realistic?"
07:50 Luis Ortega: "If you need firm 500ms p95 at 10x, that usually requires prewarmed hotpool sized for that burst or a hybrid: reserve baseline + prewarm scheduled for events. Otherwise you'll trade latency for cost. We can model costs from your trace and give a recommendation."
08:08 Dana Price: "Ok great. Let's move to logistics — I'll hand to Priya for security questions she wants clarified."
08:14 Priya Khatri: "Two quick ones: data residency — can we ensure inference payloads remain in our EU region? And do you keep payloads for debug?"
08:23 Maya Chen: "Yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have regional endpoints too. By default logs are retained for 30 days but we can add custom retention policies or disable logging of payloads; for debugging you can enable ephemeral logs with explicit consent."
08:38 Priya: "Thanks. Also, we need a sample DPA/BAA clause for PHI handling."
08:43 Maya Chen: "We'll include DPA and a BAA template in the doc bundle. Procurements typically ask for that up front."
08:50 Dana Price: "Cool, sounds like the plan. Next steps?"
08:54 Maya Chen: "We'll share the reserved capacity worksheet, SOC2 + architecture docs, and ask for your traces. Luis will propose benchmark dates. Priya and Samir to sync on compliance Qs. Can we aim to reconvene around 8/17 for decisioning?"
09:09 Dana Price: "Works for me. Thanks everyone."

Closing notes: customer tone positive; main blockers: procurement timeline and ensuring burst guarantee without prohibitive cost. Erythra is risk-averse on PHI and needs KMS + DPA. They are open to a Q4 pilot conditioned on benchmark results and contract terms.

Attachments referenced: reserved-capacity-worksheet.xlsx (to be sent), enterprise-compliance-binder.pdf (SOC2/ISO), benchmark-harness-instructions.md

End of transcript.
